Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order of operations can affect the rounding errors introduced at each step. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate results due to the finite precision of floating-point representation. This means that \((a + b) + c\) can yield a different result than \(a + (b + c)\).
